test_cases.title: Receive Raw NMEA Bytes from Hardware Interface
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART hardware interface preloaded with a known NMEA byte stream.
procedure: Preload mock UART RX buffer with a fixed NMEA byte sequence ending in CRLF.
Initialize the GPS library against the mock hardware interface.
Invoke the GPS library read API to retrieve available bytes.
Compare the bytes returned by the library against the preloaded byte sequence.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The library returns the exact byte sequence that was preloaded into the mock UART, byte-for-byte and in order.

test_cases.title: Verbatim Pass-Through of NMEA Sentence Bytes
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART preloaded with a complete GPGGA sentence including the asterisk, checksum, and CRLF.
procedure: Preload mock UART with the GPGGA sentence: '$GPGGA,123519,4807.038,N,01131.000,E,1,08,0.9,545.4,M,46.9,M,,*47\r\n'.
Initialize the GPS library against the mock hardware interface.
Invoke the GPS library read API to obtain the buffered sentence.
Perform a byte-by-byte comparison between the input sentence and the bytes returned by the library.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every byte returned by the library matches the corresponding byte of the preloaded sentence; no characters added, removed, or modified.

test_cases.title: Sustain 5 Hz Sentence Delivery Rate
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART that delivers a fresh NMEA sentence every 200 ms of simulated time.
procedure: Configure the mock UART to emit one full NMEA sentence per simulated 200 ms interval.
Advance simulated time by 1 second (5 sentence intervals).
Repeatedly invoke the GPS library read API, accumulating completed sentences.
Count the number of distinct sentences successfully returned within the 1 second window.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The library returns at least 5 complete NMEA sentences within the 1-second simulated interval without dropping any.

test_cases.title: Non-Blocking Read Returns Within Timeout (No Data)
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART that has no bytes available in the RX buffer.
procedure: Ensure mock UART RX buffer is empty.
Record the current monotonic timestamp T0.
Invoke the GPS library read API with a timeout of 10 milliseconds.
Record the timestamp T1 immediately upon return.
Verify the elapsed time (T1 - T0) and inspect the returned status code.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The read call returns within 10 ms +/- scheduler tolerance with a non-success status indicating no data, and never blocks indefinitely.

test_cases.title: Non-Blocking Read Returns Promptly With Data
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART preloaded with a complete NMEA sentence available immediately.
procedure: Preload mock UART with one complete NMEA sentence.
Record the current monotonic timestamp T0.
Invoke the GPS library read API with a timeout of 10 milliseconds.
Record the timestamp T1 immediately upon return.
Inspect the returned status code and the elapsed time (T1 - T0).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The read call returns success with the available bytes and elapsed time is strictly less than the 10 ms timeout.

test_cases.title: Health Indicator Reports Healthy When Data Flowing
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART that continuously emits valid NMEA sentences at 1 Hz.
procedure: Configure the mock UART to deliver a fresh NMEA sentence every 1 second.
Advance simulated time by 3 seconds while invoking the read API each interval.
Query the GPS library health indicator API.
Inspect the returned health value.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The health indicator reports the healthy / data-flowing state after multiple successful reads.

test_cases.title: Health Indicator Reports Unhealthy When Data Stops
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART that emits one NMEA sentence then goes silent.
procedure: Preload mock UART with one NMEA sentence and stop further emission.
Invoke the GPS library read API once to consume the available sentence.
Advance simulated time beyond the configured no-data threshold.
Query the GPS library health indicator API.
Inspect the returned health value.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: After the no-data threshold elapses, the health indicator transitions to the unhealthy / no-data state.

test_cases.title: Failure Status Returned on Hardware Read Error
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART that returns a hardware error code on the next read.
procedure: Configure the mock UART to fail the next read with a simulated hardware error.
Invoke the GPS library read API.
Capture the returned JUNO_STATUS_T value.
Compare the captured status against expected failure status codes.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The read API returns a non-success JUNO_STATUS_T value distinct from the no-data status when the underlying hardware reports an error.

test_cases.title: POSIX Implementation Functionally Equivalent to Pico2 API
test_cases.setup: Build the gps_lib unit tests in the POSIX configuration linking against the POSIX implementation.
procedure: Compile the gps_lib unit test binary against the POSIX implementation.
Run the full gps_lib test suite covering init, read, health, and timeout APIs.
Inspect the test runner output for pass/fail per test.
Verify the public API symbols and signatures used by tests match those documented for the Pico2 build.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All gps_lib unit tests pass against the POSIX implementation using the identical public API as the Pico2 build.

test_cases.title: WGS-84 Geodetic and HAE Fields Preserved Verbatim
test_cases.setup: Initialize GPS library with a mock UART preloaded with a GPGGA sentence containing known latitude, longitude, and HAE altitude fields.
procedure: Invoke the GPS library read API to obtain the delivered sentence.
Extract the latitude, N/S, longitude, E/W, altitude, and altitude unit substrings from the delivered bytes.
Compare each extracted substring to the original input character-for-character.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Latitude '4807.038', N indicator, longitude '01131.000', E indicator, altitude '545.4', and unit 'M' fields in the delivered sentence exactly match the input.

test_cases.title: Power-On Self-Test Detects Present GPS Receiver
test_cases.setup: Pico 2 board with FGPMMOPA6H GPS module wired to flight UART. Serial console attached at the configured FSW baud rate. Antenna connected; clear sky not required for probe.
procedure: Connect the Pico 2 USB to host and open the serial console at the configured baud rate.
Power the board with the GPS module connected and powered.
Reset the Pico 2 to trigger the FSW boot sequence.
Observe the serial console output during the POST phase.
Locate the GPS POST log line indicating presence/responsiveness of the GPS receiver.
Save the captured serial console output to 'gps_post_present.log'.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The POST log line for the GPS reports the receiver as present and responsive within the POST window after reset.

expected_artifacts.name: gps_post_present.log
expected_artifacts.description: Serial console capture from Pico 2 boot showing GPS POST result with GPS module connected.

test_cases.title: Power-On Self-Test Detects Missing GPS Receiver
test_cases.setup: Pico 2 board with the GPS module physically disconnected from the flight UART. Serial console attached at the configured FSW baud rate.
procedure: Disconnect the GPS module from the flight UART (leave power off to the GPS).
Connect the Pico 2 USB to host and open the serial console.
Reset the Pico 2 to trigger the FSW boot sequence.
Observe the serial console output during the POST phase.
Locate the GPS POST log line.
Save the captured serial console output to 'gps_post_absent.log'.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The POST log line for the GPS reports the receiver as absent or non-responsive within the POST window after reset.

expected_artifacts.name: gps_post_absent.log
expected_artifacts.description: Serial console capture from Pico 2 boot showing GPS POST failure with GPS module disconnected.

test_cases.title: Pico2 Implementation Reads NMEA from Flight UART
test_cases.setup: Pico 2 board with FGPMMOPA6H GPS module wired to the flight UART, antenna connected with clear sky view. Serial console attached. FSW image built with the Pico2 gps_lib implementation.
procedure: Place the rocket avionics outdoors with clear sky view of the antenna.
Connect serial console to Pico 2 USB at the configured baud rate.
Power the board and allow FSW to start.
Stream FSW telemetry/log output to the host for at least 60 seconds.
Confirm log entries containing raw NMEA sentences (e.g. lines beginning with '$GP' or '$GN').
Save the captured serial console output to 'gps_pico2_uart.log'.
Take a photo of the test setup showing the avionics, antenna, and GPS module.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Raw NMEA sentences sourced from the flight UART appear in the captured log within 60 seconds of FSW start.

expected_artifacts.name: gps_pico2_uart.log
expected_artifacts.description: Serial console capture showing raw NMEA sentences read by the Pico2 gps_lib implementation from the flight UART.

expected_artifacts.name: gps_pico2_setup.jpg
expected_artifacts.description: Photo of the Pico 2 + GPS module hardware setup used for the demonstration.
